audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill/Skill/Skill/Vladimir/Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir while the content whys and the packet chart both describe Sett owning Levels 1-5.
audit.why: Vladimir's only escape is Sanguine Pool, which is 28s at rank 1 against Facebreaker's 16s, so the early bracket is Sett's; Vladimir takes over from first item.
audit.corrected: Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill / Vladimir / Vladimir.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields called early Vladimir 'mana-starved' or 'mana-hungry'.
audit.why: Vladimir has no mana. Every ability in his kit costs 0; Tides of Blood (E) is paid for with his own health. Telling the player to wait out a mana bar that does not exist is a false read on his early weakness.
audit.corrected: Replaced with his real early weakness — Sanguine Pool unranked, and Tides of Blood costing him health.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and phases[4].why gave no numbers and did not state the untargetability.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool makes him untargetable for 2 seconds on a 28/25/22/19/16s cooldown — it voids The Show Stopper outright, and Transfusion falls to a 4.6s cooldown at rank 5, which is what beats chip damage without Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Untargetable window, real cooldowns and the anti-heal timing are now stated (missing interactions untargetable-dodges-burst and needs-antiheal).

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Vladimir has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool is 19-22s at these ranks and Facebreaker is 11.5-13s — your stun comes back first. Trade the moment he surfaces from the pool.

edits.before: The Show Stopper online — you can start fights Vladimir doesn't want. Suplex him into your wave or tower, never into his own minions.
edits.after: Level 6 is one button: Sanguine Pool makes him untargetable for 2s, so The Show Stopper only lands after he surfaces or after he has spent it.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Dodges your E. Bait it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool (W): 28s at rank 1 down to 16s at rank 5 — 2s untargetable, and it voids your R.

edits.before: Sett bullies a weak, mana-starved Level 1 Vladimir off the wave.
edits.after: Sett bullies a Level 1 Vladimir with no Sanguine Pool off the wave.

edits.before: This is your kill window: Vlad is weak and mana-starved early, so E-W-Q him with a full Grit bar before he can Q Transfusion enough to heal — his only escape is Sanguine Pool on a long cooldown.
edits.after: This is your kill window: Sanguine Pool (W) is 28s at rank 1, so once he burns it he has no escape for half a minute. Full Grit bar, E-stun, Haymaker — Transfusion (Q) cannot out-heal that.

edits.before: Vlad's spike (Rylai/Blackfire) turns the tide: Transfusion sustain plus Tides of Blood poke out-heal your trades, so stop all-inning and shove to deny his scaling.
edits.after: Vlad's first item flips it: Transfusion (Q) drops to 4.6s at rank 5 and out-heals your chip. Buy Executioner's before this, not after — anti-heal is what keeps the trade honest.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 you're the bully: Vlad's early Q Transfusion is weak and mana-hungry, so walk up with Grit shielding and chunk him whenever he steps to farm. Deny CS and force him to give ground.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 you're the bully: Tides of Blood (E) costs him his own health and Sanguine Pool is not ranked yet, so walk up with Grit shielding and chunk him every time he steps to last-hit.

notes: Vladimir is manaless — three fields claimed otherwise and are corrected. Whether Sanguine Pool can be cast while suppressed by The Show Stopper is not answerable from the kit data and was deliberately not asserted; the text only says the pool voids the ult when cast before it lands.
